items.title: Power and water desalination plant, Kuwait, Kuwait: Kuwait approved a defense cooperation agreement with Pakistan covering military training, logistics, intelligence sharing, and defense technology cooperation, without mutual defense guarantees.
items.description: Kuwait approved a defense cooperation agreement with Pakistan covering military training, logistics, intelligence sharing, and defense technology cooperation, without mutual defense guarantees.
items.rawSummary: The power and water desalination plant remains under repeated Iranian attack as part of a wider campaign against Kuwaiti infrastructure, while Kuwait has denied joining offensive operations and has approved a defense cooperation agreement with Pakistan to strengthen its defensive capabilities.
items.analysis: Iran’s repeated targeting of critical infrastructure in Kuwait, including the power and water desalination plant, continues as a deliberate effort to impose civilian and economic costs and compel Kuwait to curtail US military operations. In recent days, Iran’s army announced new waves of drone attacks on US military facilities, Kuwaiti air defenses have been intercepting hostile targets fired from Iran, and strikes have broadened to border crossings and Bubiyan Island. The attacks occur alongside Iranian claims of destroying US air defense systems in Jordan and an IRGC message accusing Washington of violating Kuwait’s sovereignty. Kuwait has since denied a Wall Street Journal report that it joined operations against Iran, with its ambassador stating that Kuwaiti territory, airspace, and waters have not been used for offensive actions. While air defenses remain active and the electricity grid has been stable under conservation, some installations have sustained heavy damage, and Reuters reported that Russia may be providing Iran with targeting intelligence, while President Trump signaled he may expand US strikes on Iran, raising the risk of escalation. In a further sign of its efforts to bolster defenses, Kuwait approved a defense cooperation agreement with Pakistan, formalizing a 2023 pact on military training, logistics, intelligence sharing, and defense technology, though it includes no mutual defense guarantees.

items.title: Walter Reed National Military Medical Center, United States: Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu announced he will travel to Washington to meet President Trump and discuss the situation in Iran, among other issues.
items.description: Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu announced he will travel to Washington to meet President Trump and discuss the situation in Iran, among other issues.
items.rawSummary: Walter Reed continues to care for injured troops amid a U.S. operational pause, as new reporting reveals the severe toll the conflict has taken on American air defense inventories.
items.analysis: Walter Reed continues to care for injured troops amid a U.S. operational pause, as new reporting reveals the severe toll the conflict has taken on American air defense inventories. President Trump halted further escalation after 13 nights of strikes following warnings from senior military leaders that a larger campaign could dangerously reduce Patriot interceptor supplies needed to protect U.S. forces, as reported by The New York Times; CNN later detailed that Vice President JD Vance and Joint Chiefs Chairman Gen. Dan Caine also urged caution, citing dwindling stockpiles and risks of prolonged war. New figures from ABC and CSIS indicate that up to 80% of THAAD interceptors, more than half of SM-3s, and up to 61% of Patriots have been expended, while NBC reports that commanders are now deliberately allowing some Iranian missiles and drones to strike bases—accepting damage to runways, radars, and fuel depots—to conserve interceptors for threats headed toward troops. This resource-driven tactical shift, combined with ongoing diplomatic outreach via Oman, continued economic pressure, and an upcoming meeting between President Trump and Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu to discuss Iran, defines the uncertain operational environment in which Walter Reed functions; the medical center is likely to continue receiving casualties if hostilities resume or if attacks on U.S. installations increase.

This resource-driven tactical shift, combined with ongoing diplomatic outreach via Oman, continued economic pressure, and an upcoming meeting between President Trump and Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu to discuss Iran, defines the uncertain operational environment in which Walter Reed functions; the medical center is likely to continue receiving casualties if hostilities resume or if attacks on U.S. installations increase.

items.analysis: U.S. intelligence assesses that Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei is more willing than his father to pursue nuclear weapons, though Iran has not resumed its program. The U.S. paused airstrikes for a second straight night, and Iran's Army spokesman said Tehran suspended retaliatory strikes after the pause, warning any resumption would widen the war geographically as the conflict already spread to the Bab el-Mandeb. This pause, alongside Oman-mediated talks on reopening the Strait of Hormuz, marks a tentative de-escalation, even as President Trump threatened further military action. Iran's IRGC spokesperson claimed that during the ceasefire Iran increased capabilities, accelerated missile production, and improved missile accuracy, while asserting the U.S. was unable to compensate for its oil deficit. Meanwhile, Iran's unverified claims of extensive damage to U.S. assets, refinement of Kheibar Shekan missiles, new drone capabilities, and domestic hardline pressure against negotiations underline the persistent volatility that keeps Parchin at the center of tensions over leadership's nuclear ambitions.
